association_basis: Geometry recomputed. SN.1/Circ.336 annex 2 (SRC-2254, WGS 84) gives precautionary area Dangan Channel No. 2, part of the Dangan Channel TSS (COLREG.2/Circ.71), as the polygon (6) 22°08'.31N 114°15'.31E, (19) 22°08'.91N 114°14'.16E, (20) 22°08'.91N 114°12'.04E, (13) 22°08'.51N 114°11'.77E, (16) 22°06'.80N 114°11'.77E, (7) 22°06'.60N 114°15'.31E. The State Council HKSAR boundary coordinates (SRC-2255, WGS 84) include point 18 at 22°08'54.5"N 114°14'09.6"E (22°08'.91N 114°14'.16E) and point 19 at 22°08'18.8"N 114°15'18.6"E (22°08'.31N 114°15'.31E). Points 17 and 18 run along the parallel 22°08'54.5"N. So TSS vertices (19) and (6) coincide with HKSAR boundary points 18 and 19 to 0.01', and vertex (20) lies on the boundary parallel. The northern edge of the TSS is the HKSAR boundary. Hong Kong VTS applies within Hong Kong waters (SRC-2256, SRC-2257), with sectors drawn to the HKSAR boundary. The HK Marine Department 2003 paper (SRC-2258) states that parts of the Dangan precautionary areas and lanes lie within Hong Kong waters, with the HK VTC serving vessels inside HKSAR waters. A 2026 report (SRC-2259) says precautionary area No. 2 connects with the East Lamma Channel TSS section. Official Guangdong MSA material, 6 March 2025 (SRC-2260, 'Guangdong Maritime' government account, article supplied by Guangzhou MSA), is about the Dangan Channel TSS. It illustrates the TSS waters with a 'Guangzhou MSA VTS radar screenshot' ('广州海事局VTS雷达截图') of fishing vessels in the area. It tells ships to strengthen contact with the VTS and, in emergencies, to call Guangzhou VTS on VHF 08/09. That is shore monitoring of the TSS by a VTS centre, which counts under decision 1. A China News Service report of 8 April 2026 (SRC-2259; photograph supplied by Guangzhou MSA; the Guangzhou VTS Centre director is quoted) says the 'Dangan' station entered trial operation to bring the Dangan Channel TSS under routine VTS control ('常态化VTS管控').

The HK VTS boundary therefore neither clearly includes nor clearly excludes it. The official HK MD 2003 paper says parts of the scheme lie inside Hong Kong waters and are served by the HK VTC. The adopted 2018 IMO geometry puts the scheme's northern edge on the boundary line rather than across it. Both readings have official support. Flag INCLUDED_BY_DEFAULT_ON_CONFLICT. This splices FC-B's VTS-0028 finding into the register, but at Boundary only, not Partial. The formal Guangzhou VTS area, per the service guide reproduced by a third party (V-S12), has outer line L1 meeting the Dangan waterway at 22°08'54.5"N 113°57'30"E. That is about 8 nm west of the TSS's western part (about 114°06'E per FC-B) and about 13 nm west of precautionary area No. 2 (114°11'.77E). The 2026 report itself says key ships bound for Hong Kong were previously outside VTS coverage, and the Dangan station is in trial, not formal, operation. Against that, the official 2025 MSA material shows Guangzhou VTS radar imaging the TSS waters and directs TSS traffic to Guangzhou VTS. Official material shows monitoring while the defined area does not reach the TSS. Flag INCLUDED_BY_DEFAULT_ON_CONFLICT. The full COLREG.2/Circ.71 annex was not retrieved (the ics.org.ir copy failed), so the lane edges west and east of precautionary area No. 2 were not tested against the boundary. Only precautionary area No. 2 was plotted. If a lane edge crosses north of 22°08'54.5"N, coverage would become Partial and the outcome INCLUDE. No MSA navigation notice or VTS area announcement extending the Guangzhou VTS area (or defining a Dangan sector) was found, and there is no confirmation that trial operation has become formal operation. The mainland and HK parts sit on either side of the HKSAR boundary. This record takes no view on jurisdiction beyond the published boundary. official_service_name: Panama Canal Authority Marine Traffic Control (Canal VTMS), Pacific entrance: Flamenco Signal Station (Port Entry Coordinator). Same ACP service as the Cristobal Signal Station link proposed for TSS-0213
rationalisation_note: Decision 7 double-check applied.
unresolved_issue: Conflict (included by default): The official sources disagree on extent and character, as they did for TSS-0213. (a) Supporting the link: ACP N-2-2026 requires the Flamenco call, and has Flamenco begin anchorage allocation and traffic coordination, at 8 nm from the Sea Buoy. That point falls on the inner end of the TSS (inner points 7.56-7.92 nm from the buoy; the ring is 0.08-0.46 nm down the lanes). NGA Pub. 153 describes this reporting chain, starting south of the TSS at Punta Mala, as the Panama Canal VTMS. NGA Pub. 148 says the same VTMS 'covers the approaches to Colon'. (b) Against the link: ACP calls Flamenco a signal station, not a VTS, and states no service area or radar coverage. The Canal operating area is described as 'the Pacific entrance and its anchorage areas'. The southernmost anchorage limit (8°49'55"N, art. 37.3.b) is 5.05-5.89 nm north of the TSS inner points. ACP N-1-2026 para 32.d treats Canal waters as beginning no further out than 3 nm from the Sea Buoy, which puts the TSS 4.6-4.9 nm outside them. The 8 nm call is a reporting point, not a stated control boundary. (c) The margin (0.08-0.44 nm) is small relative to the imprecision of an 8 nm call ring measured from a floating buoy, and the 'about 11 nm from Flamenco' gloss. So whether ACP traffic control reaches the TSS depends on which reading is taken. Official sources support either reading, so decision 7 applies. Classed as Supplemental (traffic control, not a formal VTS), with coverage limited to the inner end. Flag INCLUDED_BY_DEFAULT_ON_CONFLICT. Service identity: recommend recording ONE Canal-wide ACP service, with two signal stations, for TSS-0213 and TSS-0176, not two services. The D8 new_services entry ('ACP Cristobal Signal Station / Panama Canal Marine Traffic Control (Atlantic entrance)') should be renamed and widened to cover both stations and both TSS, so TSS-0176 adds no further service. If the project instead counts each signal station as its own service, TSS-0176 becomes +1 supplemental. No ACP statement of Flamenco radar or AIS coverage extent, and no service polygon, was found. ACP N-2-2026 mentions radar only for checking anchored positions. The ACP Navigation Regulation was read from a third-party compiled copy (ARMCOL), which may predate recent amendments; the official Acuerdo 360 scan on pancanal.com is not machine-readable. official_service_name: VTS Callao (Servicio de Control del Tráfico Marítimo, TRAMAR, Callao)
association_basis: Official Peruvian sources now support the link, so NGA is no longer needed to close it; NGA stays only as corroboration, consistent with the Chilean standard. (1) Tier 1: the consolidated Reglamento of D.L. 1147 (D.S. 015-2014-DE as amended to D.S. 001-2024-DE, published by DICAPI) establishes TRAMAR as the National Maritime Authority's Maritime Traffic Control Service, operated through the harbour master 24 hours a day. It can interact with ships and respond to traffic in the area under control. Its functions include monitoring and controlling maritime traffic and ordering ship movements (arts. 159-171). Ships must notify TRAMAR on entering the control area 20 nm from the first or outer channel buoys, report again at 4 nm 'para recibir instrucciones', and report outbound at 4 and 20 nm (arts. 164, 170). (2) Tier 2: MTC (15 Sep 2024) and the Marina de Guerra del Perú (19 Sep 2024) confirm that the Callao Maritime Traffic Control Centre was re-equipped and inaugurated as 'VTS Callao'. It is administered by DICAPI, with three coastal radars and seven optronic cameras. (3) Geometry: every point of all three Callao TSS parts lies within 3.7 nm of position (24) 12°02.05'S 077°14.64'W (WGS 84), the precautionary area and ATBA at the outer fairway approach (NGA gives the traffic circle at 12°01.8'S 77°14.8'W, 0.3 nm away). The whole scheme therefore lies inside the 20 nm control-area notice and inside the 4 nm instruction report, with a margin of more than 16 nm to the notice limit. NGA Pub. 125 (lead) names the scheme 'TSS (TRAMAR)' and requires reports at 20, 10 and 4 miles and at the Outer Fairway Lighted Buoy. The service qualifies as core: it is designated VTS by the operating authority, and under decision 5 it is also an official traffic control service whose control area demonstrably contains the TSS.
rationalisation_note: Decision 7 double-check applied.
unresolved_issue: No DICAPI publication giving a VTS Callao polygon, VHF working channels or call sign was found. The control area is inferred from the Tier 1 notice distances (20 nm and 4 nm from the outer buoys), not from a published polygon. The HIDRONAV radio-aids list was not consulted. The regulation text is a DICAPI-hosted consolidated version, not the El Peruano gazette original.

tss_name: At the approaches to Puerto Cristobal
final_vts_result: NEW SERVICE CONFIRMED (included by default on conflict)
official_service_name: Panama Canal Authority Atlantic-entrance traffic control: Cristobal Signal Station (Port Entry Coordinator), part of the ACP Marine Traffic Control / VTMS
rationalisation_note: Decision 7 double-check applied.
unresolved_issue: Conflict (included by default): The sources disagree on both characterisation and extent. (a) NGA Pub. 148 says the Panama Canal VTMS covers the approaches to Colón, which on a plain reading includes the IMO 'approaches to Puerto Cristobal' TSS. NGA is the same volume type relied on for the Chilean VTS links. (b) ACP's own texts call the unit a signal station, not a VTS, and give no service area. They define the Canal operating areas as the Atlantic entrance and its anchorage areas; the outer anchorage and sea buoy end at 9°26'20"N, 1.7-5 nm south of the TSS's inner ends. (c) The ACP mandatory call point (8 nm from the breakwater in N-2-2026, against 6 miles in the Navigation Regulation art. 36 and 12 miles in NGA) falls on the inner end of the TSS, within the imprecision of an 'Atlantic Breakwater' reference whose two heads are 0.3 nm apart. So whether ACP traffic control reaches the TSS depends on which of these readings is taken. Official sources support either reading, so decision 7 applies. Classed as Supplemental (traffic control, not a formal VTS), with coverage limited to the inner end. Flag INCLUDED_BY_DEFAULT_ON_CONFLICT. No ACP statement of VTMS radar/AIS coverage or a service polygon was found. The official Acuerdo 360 text on pancanal.com is a scanned image and could not be read (no OCR available); the compiled regulation copy is a third-party host and may predate recent amendments. ACP N-1-2026 was not retrieved. The same reasoning should be applied to TSS-0176 (Flamenco Signal Station, Pacific entrance) for consistency; that TSS was not re-examined here.
